extraction_notes: TITLES ONLY: the HS Program of Studies (pp. 5-15) gives only course title, length and credits in tables; per-course descriptions live in ~150 separate linked Google Doc/Drive syllabi (per Phase 1 issues) which were NOT followed, so every course has description null, grade_levels [] and prerequisites null. Middle-school-only courses (marked 'Middle School Course') skipped; the separate middle school catalog (grades 7-8, all credits N/A) was reviewed but contributed no records. Courses marked '^^' (no legend in catalog) are noted in notes. Honors-ensemble (*) / Honors+General concurrent (*) markers in Music, Art and Woodshop recorded in notes/honors_option. Stafford Technical Center is named as a CTE sending destination with no program names, so no CTE records. Pathway options without descriptions (VTVLC, independent study, work experience, internships, exchange, Vermont Adult Learning, PE credit for varsity sports, alternative programming) are bullet-listed only and not made into records; Dual Enrollment and Early College (described on p.16) are included. 'Interconnections' is 2 credits (1 Math / 1 Elective), listed under Mathematics. 'Integrated Math 1/2 Honor' text starts 'ntegrated' (typo in PDF text) and was corrected; 'Human Anatomy & Physiology' joined from a two-line cell. Grade levels not stated per course (AP: general statement says sophomores, juniors, seniors). Source page numbers refer to the HS catalog PDF. Social Studies credit figure in grad requirements is ambiguous as printed.

courses.description: All Vermont juniors and seniors are eligible to take two courses at any of the Vermont colleges (except Middlebury College) for free. Students are strongly advised to take Introduction to College Studies prior to taking a college course. In order to take advantage of this opportunity, students must meet with their school counselor, who will help navigate the process.

courses.description: Vermont also offers free tuition for high school seniors who are admitted to one of the Vermont State College’s Early College Programs. To apply to the Early College Program, students should arrange a meeting with their parents/guardians and school counselor in the spring of their junior year.
